objective: A frozen exact census of the 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws and the atom x, y -> c: B1 which of the tree, six lines, the plane and every finite board with at most six places each law allows, with and without frozen places (predictions P1 to P3); B2 identity of indiscernibles at radius 1, whether boards exist, the largest, whether one is non-abelian and whether one is plane-like and abelian (P4); B3 the relations of the square's identity distinction e(1, xyXY) with the values along the square and their K1-K3 verdicts (a reading); B4 the truncated CNF on the ball of names by an independent SAT code for parity 0, parity 1 and the atom (P5). Stress one size past: finite boards with 7 and 8 places, radius 2, truncations L = 7 and L = 5.
title: Which boards one-bit laws allow
